result:
I graded submission s2 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 of 6 fully right, 2 partly right and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model only writes the tool request; the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | Wrong | You chose "it will eventually fix the bug" (M6). With the same failing result each step, running longer adds nothing, so the loop needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | Partial | 4 is the right count. But your reasoning says the model runs each tool itself (M4); it only writes a request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q5 | Correct | You gave both halves: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide what to do next. |
| q6 | Partial | The name helps, but the model chooses from the whole description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**Summary:** You have the loop down. Two ideas to fix are that the program runs the tools, not the model, and that an agent needs a stopping condition.

**Next step:** write a short description for `check_calendar` (what it does, its parameters, when to use it) and a step limit for the makerspace assistant. We'll use both when we start the context and memory lesson.

I also added learning record `0003` and updated `NOTES.md` with the open misconceptions. Submission s1 is still ungraded.
